nodes.label: Reverse-Lookup Glossary
nodes.rationale: Turns a vague description of a motion effect into the precise term so the user knows what to ask for. It names effects; it does not design or build them.

nodes.label: Project Vocabulary Page
nodes.rationale: The glossary is a curated snapshot of the project's /vocabulary page; the two should be kept in sync when either changes.

nodes.label: Easing
nodes.rationale: The rate at which an animation speeds up or slows down.

nodes.label: Spring Animations
nodes.rationale: Physics-based motion as an alternative to fixed-duration easing.

nodes.label: Animation Performance
nodes.rationale: What keeps motion smooth instead of stuttering.

nodes.label: Principles to Know
nodes.rationale: Concepts that guide when and how to animate.

nodes.label: Pop In
nodes.rationale: An element appears with a slight overshoot, like it bounces into place.

nodes.label: Bounce
nodes.rationale: A spring that overshoots and settles, adding playfulness.

nodes.label: Scale In
nodes.rationale: An element grows from smaller to full size as it appears, often paired with a fade.

nodes.label: Reveal
nodes.rationale: Content is uncovered gradually, often by animating a clip-path or mask.

nodes.label: Clip-path
nodes.rationale: Clipping an element to a shape, used for reveals, masks, and before/after sliders.

nodes.label: Mask
nodes.rationale: Hiding or revealing parts of an element with a shape or gradient. Like clip-path, but with soft, fadeable edges.

nodes.label: Shared Element Transition
nodes.rationale: An element travels and transforms from one position into another, like a thumbnail expanding into a card.

nodes.label: Layout Animation
nodes.rationale: When an element's size or position changes, it animates to the new spot instead of snapping.

nodes.label: Crossfade
nodes.rationale: One element fades out as another fades in, in the same spot.

nodes.label: Morph
nodes.rationale: One shape smoothly turns into another shape, for example Dynamic Island.

nodes.label: Origin-Aware Animation
nodes.rationale: An element animates out of its trigger, like a popover growing from the button that opened it, instead of from its own center, which is the CSS default.

nodes.label: Transform Origin
nodes.rationale: The anchor point a scale or rotation grows or spins from.

nodes.label: Rubber-banding
nodes.rationale: Resistance and snap-back when you drag past a boundary, the iOS overscroll feel.

nodes.label: Spring
nodes.rationale: Motion driven by physics (tension, mass, damping) rather than a set duration.

nodes.label: Stiffness / Tension
nodes.rationale: How strongly the spring pulls toward its target. Higher feels snappier.

nodes.label: Damping
nodes.rationale: How quickly a spring settles. Lower damping means more bounce and oscillation.

nodes.label: Mass
nodes.rationale: How heavy the animated element feels. More mass makes it slower and more sluggish.

nodes.label: Momentum
nodes.rationale: Motion that carries velocity, especially after a drag or interruption.

nodes.label: Velocity
nodes.rationale: How fast and in which direction an element is moving. A spring carries it into the next animation when interrupted.

nodes.label: Interruptible Animation
nodes.rationale: An animation that can be smoothly redirected mid-flight instead of finishing first.

nodes.label: Perceptual Duration
nodes.rationale: How long a spring feels finished, even though it keeps micro-settling underneath.

nodes.label: Stagger
nodes.rationale: Animate several items one after another with a small delay between each, creating a cascade.

nodes.label: Ease-out
nodes.rationale: Starts fast, ends slow. The default for most UI and anything responding to the user.

nodes.label: Ease-in
nodes.rationale: Starts slow, ends fast. Usually avoided because it can feel sluggish.

nodes.label: Ease-in-out
nodes.rationale: Slow, fast, slow. Good for elements already on screen moving from A to B.

nodes.label: Linear Easing
nodes.rationale: Constant speed. Avoid for UI; reserve for spinners or marquees.

nodes.label: Cubic-bezier
nodes.rationale: A custom easing curve defined for precise control.

nodes.label: Keyframes
nodes.rationale: Defined points in an animation that the browser fills the gaps between.

nodes.label: Spatial Consistency
nodes.rationale: Animate so an element keeps its identity and position across states, so users never lose track of where things went.

nodes.label: Purposeful Animation
nodes.rationale: Motion should serve a function — orient, give feedback, or show relationships — not just decorate.

nodes.label: Frequency of Use
nodes.rationale: The more often a user sees an animation, the shorter and subtler it should be.

nodes.label: Perceived Performance
nodes.rationale: The right animation makes an interface feel faster, even when it is not.

nodes.label: Reduced Motion
nodes.rationale: Respect the user's prefers-reduced-motion setting by toning down or removing motion.

nodes.label: Hardware Acceleration
nodes.rationale: Animating transform and opacity lets the GPU keep motion smooth.

nodes.label: Layout Thrashing
nodes.rationale: Animating width, height, top, or left forces layout recalculation every frame and causes jank.

nodes.label: Compositing
nodes.rationale: Letting the GPU move or fade an element on its own layer without redoing layout or paint.

nodes.label: will-change
nodes.rationale: A CSS hint that an element is about to animate, so the browser can promote it to its own layer ahead of time.

nodes.label: Jank
nodes.rationale: Visible stutter when the browser drops frames because it cannot keep up with the animation.

nodes.label: Press / Tap Feedback
nodes.rationale: A subtle scale-down when an element is clicked, so it feels physical.

nodes.label: Swipe to Dismiss
nodes.rationale: Dragging an element off-screen to close it, like a drawer or toast.

nodes.label: Drag
nodes.rationale: Moving an element by grabbing it, often with momentum when released.

nodes.label: Parallax
nodes.rationale: Background and foreground move at different speeds while scrolling, creating depth.

nodes.label: Hold to Confirm
nodes.rationale: A progress effect that fills up while the user holds a button.

nodes.label: Blur
nodes.rationale: A blur filter used to soften an element or mask tiny imperfections.

nodes.label: Anticipation
nodes.rationale: A small wind-up in the opposite direction before a move, hinting at what is about to happen.

nodes.label: Follow-through
nodes.rationale: Parts of an element keep moving and settle slightly after the main motion stops, adding weight.

nodes.label: Squash and Stretch
nodes.rationale: Deforming an element as it moves to convey weight, speed, and flexibility.
